claims.text: Modified transition metal dichalcogenides will exhibit greater HER catalytic activity than traditional platinum-based catalysts.
Modified transition metal dichalcogenides will exhibit greater HOR catalytic activity than traditional platinum-based catalysts.
Modified transition metal dichalcogenides will be more durable during HER than traditional platinum-based catalysts.
Modified transition metal dichalcogenides will be more durable during HOR than traditional platinum-based catalysts.
MoS2 and WS2 in basal-plane form are candidate transition metal dichalcogenide starting materials.
Metal nanoparticle modification or elemental doping enhances the electronic properties of TMDs.
The layered structure of TMDs increases the number of catalytically active sites.
Doping or metal nanoparticle decoration modifies the electronic structure of TMDs.
The modified electronic structure enhances charge transfer.
The modified electronic structure increases active-site availability.
Modified TMDs will produce lower HER and HOR overpotentials than platinum catalysts.
Modified TMDs will have longer HER and HOR operational lifetimes than platinum catalysts.
The proposed performance enhancement applies in acidic or alkaline electrochemical environments at room temperature.
